rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November). So does a list of creature types: "any Undead, Fey, or Elemental".

data.title: The Great Game: Intrigue in the Courts of Europe
data.where: The courts of Europe, and Mutapa's service in them
data.read_with: Powers and Factions; in The State of the World, Europe, and Mutapa and the Indian Ocean
data.summary: **The pitch.** In 1668 every ministry of magic in Europe has learned two things: it is behind Mutapa, and Spain has Mutapa's metal in the Chocó (see The World in 1668). The Great Game is the espionage that follows, played with licenses, portraits and shewstones by the spymasters who are this setting's secret heroes, and the party is one of their crews.
hooks: A court painter has finished a miniature of the young King of Spain for the Emperor's court, and Louis's ambassador wants a look at it before it reaches Vienna.
A Viennese clerk has been copying the Emperor's register of licensed casters for another court; whoever catches him first will use him rather than hang him.
A shewstone pair given by Mutapa has started answering in a voice that isn't the other stone's.
An Agitator cell inside the Invisible College has a scheme for the Grand Divertissement; a natural philosopher among them has doubts.
A Mutapan lamp in a minister's study has been opened and closed again, and the guild's mark on its base is now upside down.
Mutapa's spymaster wants to know who told Spain what its platina was: the letter came from Lisbon, in excellent Portuguese.
Anselme Lafrenaye, the Gamester of the French court, has lost a hand he couldn't have lost, to a man who shouldn't have known the odds.

data.title: The Venice Job
data.summary: **The pitch.** The Republic of Venice is about to sell the most wanted document in Europe, and a crew can be paid to take it before the sale. Venice is losing Candia in the twenty-first year of the siege and will sell anything it has, and a desperate state with the best scryers and cipher clerks in Europe makes mistakes. The city is the whole dungeon: canals, rooftops, palaces and archives, a population that informs on itself and a fair where everyone is masked, which helps a burglar and hurts a scryer. The default date is the Sensa, the Ascension fair of May 1668, when the Doge weds the sea and the masks come out; for Carnival, run it in the winter of 1669. Its roof-runner is Zanetta Bon, a Danae of the Crossing, who folds space to cross a canal at a step (Europe, People, in The State of the World).
data.ready: **Ready to run.** *The Venice Job: The First Night* is the heist's opening night as a one-shot, with five 3rd-level characters ready to play.
hooks: The Ten are selling their scryers' report by sealed bid on the last night of the Sensa fair; the French bidder has debts and bravos; the Spanish one hires a crew.
The scryer who made the report left notes the Ten's clerks didn't understand, and Spain's ambassador is looking for her.
A health pass for a ship from Sofala has been forged, and the real ship is at the Lazzaretto with something in its hold.
The golem has stopped a man who is of the ghetto, and won't say why.
A Danae roof-runner will take the job for one price: her own file from the Ten's archive.
A denunciation has gone into a lion's mouth naming one of the party for unlicensed magic; the Ten's men come at dawn.

data.title: The Border: The Village and the Hidden
data.where: Any village at the edge of the Hidden
data.read_with: Running Euphonia; *Euphonia: Life on the Border*
data.summary: The frontier game belongs to no region: every society has villages on its outskirts and a Hidden past them. The Border can be a Highland glen, a Japanese mountain village, a Swedish chapelry in the year the Blåkulla trials begin, or the almost suburban edge of one of Mutapa's fast-growing cities, where modern artifice meets the water spirits of the pools (The State of the World, Mutapa and the Indian Ocean). Pick the border your table knows.
data.ready: **Ready to run.** *The Night the Hunt Came* is a one-shot for the resisters: one dark-half night in the Border village of Bowden, with four 5th-level characters ready to play.
hooks: A child says she was carried to a feast inside a hill, and the examiner who comes to hear it is looking for witches.
The village's Killer is seventy and her knees are going.
A Mutapan survey crew has pegged out a new street across a pool that belongs to someone.
One of the taken came home last night, ten years gone and not a day older, and she has brought someone back with her.

data.title: The Tomb Road: Robbing the Dead of Four Dynasties
data.summary: A campaign of delves through China's royal dead. A party starts in a minor Ming prince's sealed tomb, in a valley the Qing ignore, and years later ends in the First Emperor's, with its rivers of mercury and its crossbows set for intruders. Between lie the tombs the DM builds: the Han and Tang dead with their tomb-quelling beasts, the alchemists' graves full of cinnabar.
hooks: A county magistrate has found a sealed door in a quarry and wants it opened, inventoried and closed again before his superior hears of it.
A loyalist society in Suzhou will pay for a prince's jade seal, and won't say which prince.
The tomb robbers of a Henan village went into a hill a month ago and haven't come out, and their families want them, or their shares, back.

data.title: The High Ground: The Andean War
data.summary: **The pitch.** The conquest never finished. A century after the huacas, the Andes' holy beings, rose, the Sapa Inca rules from Cusco again, Spain holds the coast and the silver mountain, and the line between them runs across the roof of the world. This is the war the rest of the world is about to join: whoever breaks the Andean siege, or robs Spain while it's pinned, decides who gets the metals that are turning the balance of magic. A three-sided war: the Inca, the Spanish and the people profiting off both. At stake: silver, mercury, guano, cinchona, the platina in the Chocó's rivers and the huacas that rose. It's the book's grittiest setting: Andeans defending their home, or amoral soldiers of fortune in the *Wages of Fear* vein. The Inca aren't simply the good side: their state was itself an empire built on conquest, and the Cañari and Chachapoya fought beside Spain against it.
hooks: The keepers of Pariacaca say the mountain will close the pass to Spain for a season, if someone brings back what the extirpators carried off to Lima.
A mule train of Huancavelica mercury is three days late into Potosí, and the huaca above the road has asked for something it hasn't asked for before.
The Salcedos' last silver shipment left Laicacota the week the viceroy's column arrived, and it never reached Lima.
A Spanish officer wants guides over the pass; the guide he hires has already been paid by the Sapa Inca to lose him.
In Lima, the countess's confessor is passing letters to someone on the high ground, and the letters are written in Quechua.
An English captain at Port Royal has a commission, a chart of the Atrato and no idea who drew the chart.
A Mutapan factor in Buenos Aires is buying cinchona bark at any price, more than every fever on the Zambezi could use, and nobody knows why.

data.title: The Monsoon Road: Trading the Indian Ocean Coast
data.where: The Indian Ocean, from the Cape to Macau and out into the Pacific
data.read_with: Mutapa and the Indian Ocean; Powers and Factions, Mutapa's Institutions
data.summary: **The pitch.** The players are traders: a ship, a cargo and a living to make on the monsoon winds. The game is the voyage, the ports, the deals and what a cargo is worth two harbors on. The Indian Ocean in 1668 is the world's busiest sea, and no one owns it. The Portuguese hold forts and are losing them, Oman's fleets are taking them, the Dutch hold the spice islands and search every hold in the straits, the Gujarati houses finance half the trade by *hundi*, and Mutapa holds the gold port at Sofala and the gate at the Cape. A ship out of Sofala can carry what every port wants and no one else can make: Mutapan curiosities under the guild's stamp, legal in every harbor that honors the Bird's paper. The campaign's question arrives the first time someone offers the party more for the same cargo without the stamp.
hooks: A Surat shroff will honor the party's letter on the Bird only if they carry a sealed *hundi* to Mocha and bring back the answer before the coast closes.
Robert Knox's family has paid a factor in Surat to get a letter to him in Kandy. The king reads everything that comes up the mountain, and the factor hasn't mentioned that.
The guild's crate in the hold hums at the flood, and the journeyman minding it has started sleeping on top of it.
The Omani squadron that sacked Diu is watering at Pate and wants a pilot who knows Fort Jesus by night. The fort's captain would pay more to learn the date.
A deckhand who signed on at Sofala under one name is on the guild's rolls under another, and listed as dead.
At Hoerikwaggo, a French captain offers the party a fortune to carry his returns past the harbor master's fee, and the harbor master is a friend.
The toll over the deep off Pemba was a song last voyage. This voyage it is the ship's name.
